output.headline: Hoisted by his rivals, Antonelli completes record-breaking title charge
output.standfirst:
• 20-year-old seals title with third place and four races to spare

  • Verstappen wins race ahead of Hamilton
output.bodyHtml:
Kimi Antonelli was hoisted on to the shoulders of Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen on the Mexico City podium, tears of joy marking the moment the 20-year-old became Formula One's youngest world champion, and the first Italian to take the crown since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

The title also ends a six-year wait for Mercedes, who last won the drivers' championship with Hamilton in 2020 and collected their 10th constructors' title this year. Antonelli, promoted into Hamilton's old seat only last season after a difficult rookie year, sealed it with third place at the Mexican Grand Prix, a race won by Red Bull's Verstappen from Hamilton's Ferrari, with Hamilton's teammate Charles Leclerc fourth.

Related: ‘He’s done an insane job’: Antonelli’s rivals united in praise for ‘incredible’ champion

Antonelli said the day would live with him for ever but had left him almost speechless. His race engineer, Peter Bonnington, said: “It is a very special day, a young man has broken the record for the youngest world champion. It is the first of many I reckon, I am just super happy for him, stoked.”

He becomes the sport's 36th world champion, in only his second F1 season, with four races still to go. Sebastian Vettel had been the previous youngest champion, aged 23 in 2010, when Antonelli was four.

Antonelli has led since finishing third in Japan, round three of the season, and made the most of an early-season Mercedes advantage under the new regulations, winning five of the first six races and outracing his teammate George Russell, the pre-season favourite. He went on to take nine wins, failing to score points only twice, both times through mechanical failures, and held his lead even as Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull pushed Mercedes hard, including a win from 19th on the grid at his home race in Monza.

Russell and Hamilton, his nearest rivals, needed to win in Mexico to keep the title race alive, but Antonelli's third place would have clinched it regardless. He qualified only fourth but delivered what he needed — ninth place or better — with a nerveless drive true to his season's form.

The race itself was a feisty affair. Leclerc made a strong start and tried to pass Hamilton for the lead at turn four but cut the corner to do it, and did not give the place back; stewards investigated and handed him a five-second penalty, to be served in his pit stop, for gaining an advantage by leaving the track. Hamilton, left furious that his teammate had cost them a one-two finish and let Verstappen through to the lead, said: “The problem is he's got clean air and doesn't have to manage like the rest of us. He should just give the place back. The stewards are basically handing Charles this win.” Later, as the race was stopped, he added: “We've got big problems. Big, big problems.” A lively debrief awaits at Ferrari.

A red flag followed a heavy crash for Valtteri Bottas at turn one. The restart saw Hamilton move up to second and Antonelli to third — not one to settle quietly for the minimum needed, he went on to seal the title with a podium finish, where Hamilton and Verstappen lifted him on to their shoulders.

Related: Kimi Antonelli claims the Formula One crown – his season in pictures

Verstappen's own drive from fifth on the grid was hugely impressive, and should buoy Red Bull heading into next season, setting up the prospect of him, Antonelli and, hopefully, Hamilton competing consistently at the front in 2027 — some consolation after missing out on the title himself.

For Mercedes, the win vindicates the faith the team placed in Antonelli, brought into their young driver programme at 12 and thrown into Hamilton's seat last year. He has adapted to Formula One's sharp end with alacrity and skill since, and after a season on top from start to finish, this fascinating, precocious talent looks unlikely to be done winning yet.
output.progress: Antonelli sealed the title with four races still to run, ending Mercedes' six-year wait for the drivers' championship.
